text.p: Argentina and Uruguay have launched the first stage of the international tender for the construction and operation of one of the longest bridges in the world across the River Plate, an official said Thursday.

A commission established by the Argentine and Uruguayan governments for the bridge from Buenos Aires to the Uruguayan town of Colonia has started selling tender specifications, comission secretary Alejandro Gelsi told Reuters.

Interested bidders must present themselves by July and those prequalified will be asked to submit their bids in November. The tender should be awarded about four months later and construction begin by mid-1998.
No government money will be spent on the bridge and the builders will be expected to recoup their investment by charging tolls to motorists.
The decision to award the tender will be made on the basis of the toll proposed by bidders.
"It has to be cheaper than other forms of transport to Uruguay," Gelsi said.
The 26-mile (41 km) bridge should cost under $1 billion to construct, he said.
The bridge will substantially reduce the distance for road transport from Buenos Aires to Uruguay's capital Montevideo and also to Brazil.
